summary: Robert Hinde studied at St John's College (~1941–1948) and Balliol College, Oxford (~1948–1950). He held a post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1950 to 1994, where he taught John Hurrell Crook.

Robert Hunter worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Aberdeen, Marischal College, and the University of Edinburgh before serving as a missionary with the Free Church of Scotland Mission from 1846 to 1855.

Robert I. Crane worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. After earning his B.A. at Duke and Ph.D. at Yale, he held posts at the University of Chicago, University of Michigan, Duke University, and Syracuse University (1968–1990).

Robert Isaac Levy worked in Indology and related fields. He was Professor of Anthropology at the University of California, San Diego (1969–1991), Research Professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (~1991–2003), and held a post at Duke.

Robert J. Miller worked in Tibetology and religious studies. He studied at the University of Michigan and the University of Washington, and held posts at the University of Washington, AIIS, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1959–1988).
Robert J. Topmiller is a scholar in history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Kentucky, where he studied under doctoral supervisor George C. Herring.

Robert Kritzer works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley under Padmanabh S. Jaini, and held posts at UC Berkeley and Kyoto Notre Dame University (attested 1999–2017).
Robert Kyd studied at the University of Edinburgh. In 1787, he founded the Acharya Jagadish Chandra Bose Indian Botanic Garden.

Robert L. Brown worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He served as a curator at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art (~1982–2014) and was a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles (~1986–2014).

Robert Lenz worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Tartu and under Franz Bopp in Berlin, later holding posts at Tallinn Cathedral School, the Russian and Austrian Academies of Sciences, Breslau, and Saint Petersburg State University (1835–1836).

Robert Lingat was an Indology and history scholar who earned his doctorate from the University of Paris. He taught law and Thai at Thammasat, the Universities of Indochina, Saigon, and Cambodia, INALCO, and the École Pratique des Hautes Études.

Robert M. Gimello was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who earned his PhD at Columbia University. He held faculty posts at the University of Arizona (~1981–2020) and Harvard University (~2004–2006).

Robert Maclagan, a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology, studied at Edinburgh, Addiscombe Military Seminary, and the Royal School of Military Engineering. He served as Principal of the Indian Institute of Technology Roorkee from 1847 to 1860.

Robert Magliola earned his Ph.D. at Princeton and worked in philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Purdue, Tamkang University, Assumption University, Columbia University, and National Taiwan University.

Robert Mason Towers was a scholar in Indology and linguistics who studied at Trinity College Dublin. He served as Professor of Bengali at King's College London (1888) and University Teacher at the University of Cambridge (1897–1907).

Robert Mayer is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bristol and Leiden under Tilmann Vetter, Alexis Sanderson, and Pieter Cornelis Verhagen, and held a post at the University of Oxford in 2002.

Robert Needham Cust worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Eton, Trinity College Cambridge, Haileybury, Fort William, and Edinburgh, and served in the Bengal Civil Service from circa 1843 to 1867.
Robert Orme worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Harrow School until 1741 and served as Historiographer to the East India Company from 1769 to 1801.

Indologist Robert P. Goldman studied at Columbia and under Ludo Rocher at the University of Pennsylvania (Ph.D.). He also studied with T. S. Srinivasa Sastri and S. D. Joshi, later joining the University of California, Berkeley faculty.

Robert P. Scharlemann worked in religious studies and philosophy. He studied at Concordia College, Concordia Seminary, and Heidelberg University, later holding faculty posts at USC (~1963–1966), the University of Iowa (~1966–1981), and the University of Virginia (~1981–1999).
